stemBlocks.value: Several rays meet at O on a horizontal straight line. The three angles above the line are (2x + 10)°, (x + 20)° and 3x°. a) Determine the value of x. b) Calculate the size of each of the three labelled angles above the line. c) The angle z is vertically opposite the angle (2x + 10)°. Determine z and state the relevant angle fact.
Think first: Angles on one side of a straight line always add to 180°, and that single sentence gives you the equation.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p163-q01 from workbook page 163.

solutionSteps.instruction: Write the angle equation for the straight line.

contentBlocks.value: z is vertically opposite the 60° angle

strategyBlocks.value: Set the three expressions equal to 180°, solve for x, substitute back for each angle, then use the vertically-opposite property for z.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) x = 25  (b) (2x + 10)° = 60°, (x + 20)° = 45°, 3x° = 75°  (c) z = 60°, because vertically opposite angles are equal

whyThisWorks.value: Angles that sit side by side along a straight line make a half turn, which is 180°, so writing their sum as 180 is not a guess but a definition. When two straight lines cross, each pair of opposite angles is the supplement of the same neighbouring angle, so those opposite angles must be equal — that is the vertically opposite angle fact used for z.

commonErrors.misconception: Setting the sum to 360° instead of 180°.

commonErrors.misconception: Finding x and stopping, without substituting back to give the actual angles.
